Challenges to the economy include halting or reversing the decline in per-capita income, improving education to prepare youth for the workforce and providing them with employment, diversifying the economy, stimulating the private sector and housing construction, and diminishing corruption and inequality.
The ___E:Organization of Petroleum Exporting Countries U:(https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/OPEC)___ (OPEC) limits its members' oil production based on their "proven reserves".

Saudi Arabia's published reserves have shown little change since 1980, with the main exception being an increase of about 100 billion barrels (1.6 × 10 10 m 3 ) between 1987 and 1988.  ___E:Matthew Simmons U:(https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Matthew_Simmons)___ has suggested that Saudi Arabia is greatly exaggerating its reserves and may soon show production declines (see ___E:peak oil U:(https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Peak_oil)___ ).

From 2003 to 2013, "several key services" were privatized—municipal water supply, electricity, telecommunications—and parts of education and health care, traffic control and car accident reporting were also privatized.

According to Arab News columnist Abdel Aziz Aluwaisheg, "in almost every one of these areas, consumers have raised serious concerns about the performance of these privatized entities."  In November 2005, Saudi Arabia was approved as a member of the ___E:World Trade Organization U:(https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/World_Trade_Organization)___ .

Negotiations to join had focused on the degree to which Saudi Arabia is willing to increase market access to foreign goods and in 2000, the government established the ___E:Saudi Arabian General Investment Authority U:(https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Saudi_Arabian_General_Investment_Authority)___ to encourage foreign direct investment in the kingdom.

Saudi Arabia maintains a list of sectors in which foreign investment is prohibited, but the government plans to open some closed sectors such as telecommunications, insurance, and power transmission/distribution over time. The government has also made an attempt at " ___E:Saudizing U:(https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Saudization)___ " the economy, replacing foreign workers with Saudi nationals with limited success.

In addition to petroleum and gas, Saudi has a significant gold mining sector in the ___E:Mahd adh Dhahab U:(https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Mahd_adh_Dhahab)___ region and significant other mineral industries, an agricultural sector (especially in the southwest) based on vegetables, fruits, dates etc. and livestock, and large number of temporary jobs created by the roughly two million annual hajj pilgrims.

Saudi Arabia has had five-year "Development Plans" since 1970. Among its plans were to launch "economic cities" (e.g. ___E:King Abdullah Economic City U:(https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/King_Abdullah_Economic_City)___ ) in an effort to diversify the economy and provide jobs. The cities will be spread around Saudi Arabia to promote diversification for each region and their economy, and the cities are projected to contribute $150 billion to the GDP.
Saudi Arabia is increasingly activating its ports in order to participate in trade between Europe and China in addition to oil transport.
To this end, ports such as Jeddah Islamic Port or King Abdullah Economic City are being rapidly expanded, and investments are being made in logistics.
The country is historically and currently part of the ___E:Maritime Silk Road U:(https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Maritime_Silk_Road)___ .

Statistics on poverty in the kingdom are not available through the UN resources because the Saudi government does not issue any.  The Saudi state discourages calling attention to or complaining about poverty.
In December 2011, the Saudi interior ministry arrested three reporters and held them for almost two weeks for questioning after they uploaded a video on the topic to YouTube.
Authors of the video claim that 22% of Saudis may be considered poor.  Observers researching the issue prefer to stay anonymous  because of the risk of being arrested.

The unexpected impact of the ___E:COVID-19 pandemic U:(https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/COVID-19_pandemic_in_Saudi_Arabia)___ on the economy, along with Saudi Arabia's poor human rights records, laid unforeseen challenges before the development plans of the kingdom, where some of the programmes under ' ___E:Vision 2030 U:(https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Saudi_Vision_2030)___ ' were also expected to be affected.

In May 2020, the ___E:Finance Minister of Saudi Arabia U:(https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Ministry_of_Finance_(Saudi_Arabia))___ admitted that the country's economy was facing a severe economical crisis for the first time in decades, because of the pandemic as well as declining global oil markets. ___E:Mohammed Al-Jadaan U:(https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Mohammed_Al-Jadaan)___ said that the country will take "painful" measures and keep all options open to deal with the impact.
In July 2024 Saudi Arabia's Renewable Energy Localisation Company (RELC) has formed three joint ventures with Chinese companies to advance the kingdom's clean energy infrastructure.

As part of Saudi Arabia's 2030 targets, the ___E:Public Investment Fund U:(https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Public_Investment_Fund)___ is actively promoting the localization of renewable energy components.
RELC, a division of the sovereign fund, facilitates partnerships between global manufacturers and Saudi private sector firms to strengthen local supply chains.

The joint ventures include partnerships with ___E:Envision Energy U:(https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Envision_Energy)___ for wind turbine components, Jinko Solar for photovoltaic cells, and Lumetech for solar photovoltaic ingots and wafers.
These initiatives aim to localize up to 75% of the components used in Saudi Arabia's renewable projects by 2030, positioning the country as a major global exporter of renewable technologies.

Saudi Minister of Economy and Planning, Faisal Al Ibrahim, emphasized Saudi Arabia's progress in global climate goals at the 2024 High-Level Political Forum for Sustainable Development in New York, citing over 80 initiatives and investments exceeding $180 billion for the country's green economy, as reported by Saudi Gazette.
He highlighted the alignment of these efforts with Vision 2030 objectives, focusing on local sustainability, sector integration, and societal advancement.

Saudi Arabia's predominantly arid environment, poor soil, and traditional nomadic lifestyle have long favored ___E:pastoralism U:(https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Pastoralism)___ , particularly of camels, sheep, and goats; agricultural production has historically been localised and oriented towards ___E:basic subsistence U:(https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Subsistence_agriculture)___ .
Less than two percent of the total land area is used for crops, with agriculture constituting only a fraction of GDP (2.5 percent) and employing a similar proportion of the workforce.
Initial attempts to develop dairy farming on a commercial scale occurred in the ___E:Al Kharj U:(https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Al_Kharj)___ District south of Riyadh during the 1950s.

Serious large-scale agricultural development began in the 1970s,  particularly with wheat,  with the government launching an extensive programme to promote modern farming technology; establish rural roads, irrigation networks and storage and export facilities; and encourage agricultural research and training institutions.
The kingdom has continued prioritizing domestic food production through subsidies and generous incentives.

Owing to these efforts, there has been substantial growth in the production of all basic foods: Although it still imports the bulk of its food needs, Saudi Arabia is self-sufficient in several commodities, particularly wheat, meat, milk, and eggs. The country exports dates, dairy products, eggs, fish, poultry, fruits, vegetables, and flowers.

Dates, which are indigenous to Saudi Arabia and a traditional staple of its diet, are now mainly grown for global humanitarian aid; the kingdom is the world's ___E:second largest producer U:(https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Date_palm#Production)___ after Egypt, producing 1.6 million tonnes as of 2022. Another indigenous crop, the olive, is also heavily cultivated: The ___E:Al Jouf region U:(https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Al-Jawf_Province)___ has millions of olive trees—including the world's largest olive farm at 7,713 hectares  —and the number is expected to increase to 20 million trees.
Saudi farmers also grow substantial amounts of other grains such as barley, sorghum, and millet.

Saudi Arabia has some of the most modern and largest dairy farms in the Middle East; milk production boasts a productive annual rate of 6,800 litres (1,800 US gallons) per cow, one of the highest in the world.

Saudi dairy company ___E:Almarai U:(https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Almarai)___ is the largest vertically integrated dairy company in the Middle East,  and the largest dairy firm in the world by volume;  it operates the world's largest dairy farm at Al Safi.

Following an end to domestic wheat production in 2016 to preserve water,  Saudi Arabia encouraged small famers to produce wheat in 2019 through a domestic production program established under the Saudi Ministry of Environment, Water, and Agriculture (MEWA).

In 2025, wheat production is forecast to more than double the five-year average,  with the aim of allowing up to 5,000 small farmers to produce a maximum of 1.5 million metric tons (MT) per year through 2029.

Consuming nonrenewable groundwater resulted in the loss of an estimated four-fifths of the total groundwater reserves by 2012.  About half the arable land is cultivated through ___E:rain-fed dry farming U:(https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Dryland_farming)___ (mostly in ___E:Asir U:(https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Asir)___ ), two-fifths through the planting of local tree crops (namely dates and olives), and the remainder by irrigation, mostly by underground water.

As part of the Saudi Green Initiative, which seeks to restore vegetation cover and ecological sustainability, the kingdom aims to plant 100 million ___E:mangroves U:(https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Mangrove)___ ; as of 2024, the National Centre for Vegetation Cover Development and Combating Desertification announced it had planted 13 million seedlings.
One of the main challenges for Saudi Arabia is ___E:water scarcity U:(https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Water_scarcity)___ .

Substantial investments have been undertaken in seawater ___E:desalination U:(https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Desalination)___ , water distribution, sewerage and ___E:wastewater treatment U:(https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Wastewater_treatment)___ .
Today about 50% of drinking water comes from desalination, 40% from the mining of non-renewable groundwater, and 10% from surface water in the mountainous southwest of the country.
Saudi Arabia is suffering from a major depletion of the water in its underground aquifers and a resultant break down and disintegration of its agriculture as a consequence.
As a result of the catastrophe, Saudi Arabia has bought agricultural land in the United States,   Argentina,  and Africa.
Saudi Arabia ranked as a major buyer of agricultural land in foreign countries.

According to the ___E:Joint Monitoring Programme U:(https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Joint_Monitoring_Programme_for_Water_Supply_and_Sanitation)___ (JMP) for Water Supply and Sanitation of the ___E:WHO U:(https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/WHO)___ and ___E:UNICEF U:(https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/UNICEF)___ , the latest reliable source on access to water and sanitation in Saudi Arabia is the 2004 census.
It indicates that 97% of the population had access to an improved source of drinking water and 99% had access to ___E:improved sanitation U:(https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Improved_sanitation)___ .
For 2015, the JMP estimates that access to sanitation increased to 100%.
Sanitation was primarily through on-site solutions, and about 40% of the population was connected to sewers.
In 2015, 886,000 people lacked access to "improved" water.
In 2019, Saudi Arabia adopted a general tourism ___E:travel visa U:(https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Travel_visa)___ to allow non-Muslims to visit.
Although most tourism largely involves religious pilgrimages, there is growth in the leisure tourism sector.
According to the ___E:World Bank U:(https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/World_Bank)___ , approximately 14.3 million people visited Saudi Arabia in 2012, making it the world's 19th-most-visited country.

Tourism is an important component of the ___E:Saudi Vision 2030 U:(https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Saudi_Vision_2030)___ , and according to a report conducted by ___E:BMI Research U:(https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/BMI_Research)___ in 2018 both religious and non-religious tourism have significant potential for expansion.
The kingdom offers an electronic visa for foreign visitors to attend sports events and concerts.
In 2019, the kingdom announced its plans to open visa applications for visitors, where people from about 50 countries would be able to get tourist visas to Saudi.
In 2020 it was announced that holders of a US, UK or ___E:Schengen U:(https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Schengen_Area)___ visa are eligible for a Saudi electronic visa upon arrival.
Saudi Arabia's reported population is 32,175,224 as of 2022,  making it the fourth most populous country in the ___E:Arab world U:(https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Arab_world)___ .
Close to 42% of its inhabitants are immigrants,  mostly from the Middle East, Asia, and Africa.
The Saudi population has grown rapidly since 1950, when it was estimated at 3 million.

For much of the 20th century, the country had one of the highest population growth rates in the world, at around 3% annually;  it continues to grow at a rate of 1.62% per year,  slightly higher than the rest of the Middle East and North Africa.
Consequently, the Saudi ___E:people are quite young U:(https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Youth_in_Saudi_Arabia)___ by global standards, with over half the population under 25 years old.
The ethnic composition of Saudi citizens is 90% ___E:Arab U:(https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Arab)___ and 10% ___E:Afro-Arab U:(https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Afro-Arab)___ .
Most Saudis are concentrated in the southwest; Hejaz, which is the most populated region,  is home to one-third of the population, followed by neighbouring Najd (28%) and the Eastern Province (15%).

As late as 1970, most Saudis lived a subsistence life in the rural provinces, but in the last half of the 20th century, the kingdom has urbanized rapidly: as of 2023, about 85% of Saudis live in urban metropolitan areas—specifically Riyadh, Jeddah, and Dammam.

As recently as the early 1960s, Saudi Arabia's slave population was estimated at 300000 .  ___E:Slavery U:(https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/History_of_slavery_in_the_Muslim_world)___ was officially abolished in 1962.
The official language is ___E:Arabic U:(https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Arabic)___ .

There are four main regional dialect groups spoken by Saudis: ___E:Najdi U:(https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Najdi_Arabic)___ (about 14.6 million speakers  ), ___E:Hejazi U:(https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Hejazi_Arabic)___ (about 10.3 million speakers  ), ___E:Gulf U:(https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Gulf_Arabic)___ (about 0.96 million speakers  ) including ___E:Baharna dialects U:(https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Bahrani_Arabic)___ , and Southern Hejaz and Tihama  dialects. ___E:Faifi U:(https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Faifi_language)___ is spoken by about 50000 .

The ___E:Mehri language U:(https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Mehri_language)___ is also spoken by around 20000 ___E:Mehri U:(https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Mehri_people)___ citizens.  ___E:Saudi Sign Language U:(https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Saudi_Sign_Language)___ is the principal language of the deaf community, amounting to around 100000 speakers.

The large expatriate communities also speak their own languages, the most numerous of which, according to 2018 data, are ___E:Bengali U:(https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Bengali_language)___ (~1 500000 ), ___E:Tagalog U:(https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Tagalog_language)___ (~ 900000 ), ___E:Punjabi U:(https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Punjabi_language)___ (~ 800000 ), ___E:Urdu U:(https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Urdu)___ (~ 740000 ), ___E:Egyptian Arabic U:(https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Egyptian_Arabic)___ (~ 600000 ), ___E:Rohingya U:(https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Rohingya_language)___ , ___E:North Levantine Arabic U:(https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/North_Levantine_Arabic)___ (both ~ 500000 )  and ___E:Malayalam U:(https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Malayalam)___ .
Virtually all Saudi inhabitants ___E:are Muslim U:(https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Islam_in_Saudi_Arabia)___ ;    by law, all Saudi citizens are Muslim.

Estimates of the ___E:Sunni U:(https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Sunni)___ population range between 85% and 90%, with the remaining 10 to 15% being ___E:Shia Muslim U:(https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Shia_Islam_in_Saudi_Arabia)___ ,     practicing either ___E:Twelver Shi'ism U:(https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Twelver_Shi%27ism)___ or ___E:Sulaymani Ismailism U:(https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Sulaymani)___ . ___E:Shia Muslims in Saudi Arabia U:(https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Shia_Islam_in_Saudi_Arabia)___ are largely found in the ___E:Eastern Province U:(https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Eastern_Province,_Saudi_Arabia)___ , particularly in ___E:Qatif U:(https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Qatif)___ and ___E:Al–Ahsa U:(https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Al-Ahsa_Governorate)___ .

The official and dominant form of Sunni Islam is ___E:Salafism U:(https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Salafism)___ , commonly known as ___E:Wahhabism U:(https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Wahhabism)___ ,   [h] which was founded in the Arabian Peninsula by ___E:Muhammad ibn Abd al-Wahhab U:(https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Muhammad_ibn_Abd_al-Wahhab)___ in the 18th century.
Other denominations, including ___E:Shia Islam U:(https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Shia_Islam)___ , are systematically suppressed.

___E:Christianity is the second largest religion in Saudi Arabia U:(https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Christianity_in_Saudi_Arabia)___ , estimated at around 2.1 million, of whom the vast majority are foreign workers.
Saudi Arabia allows Christians to enter the country as temporary foreign workers but does not allow them to practice their faith openly.

There are officially no Saudi citizens who are Christians,  as Saudi Arabia forbids religious conversion from Islam ( ___E:apostasy U:(https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Apostasy_in_Saudi_Arabia)___ ) and punishes it by death.

There are over 708,000 ___E:Hindus in Saudi Arabia U:(https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Hinduism_in_Saudi_Arabia)___ , comprising the third largest religion; like other minority faiths in the country, almost all foreign workers.

There may be a significant fraction of ___E:atheists U:(https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Atheism)___ and ___E:agnostics U:(https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Agnosticism)___ ,   although they are officially called "terrorists".
In its 2017 religious freedom report, the U.S.

State Department named Saudi Arabia a ___E:Country of Particular Concern U:(https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Country_of_Particular_Concern)___ , denoting systematic, ongoing, and egregious violations of religious freedom.

___E:Najran U:(https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Najran)___ was once home to sizeable historical local ___E:Christian U:(https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Christian_community_of_Najran)___ and ___E:Jewish communities U:(https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/History_of_the_Jews_in_Saudi_Arabia)___ .

Before the founding of ___E:Israel U:(https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Israel)___ , Najran had over 7,000 Jews,   predominantly of ___E:Yemenite Jewish U:(https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Yemenite_Jews)___ background.

Following the ___E:establishment of Israel U:(https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Establishment_of_Israel)___ and the ___E:1948 Arab–Israeli war U:(https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/1948_Arab%E2%80%93Israeli_War)___ , Jews began leaving for ___E:Yemen U:(https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Yemen)___ and from there to Israel.
By the 1970s, there were no Jews left in the country.

Education is free at all levels, although ___E:higher education U:(https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Higher_education_in_Saudi_Arabia)___ is restricted to citizens only.  The school system is composed of ___E:elementary, intermediate, and secondary schools U:(https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/List_of_schools_in_Saudi_Arabia)___ .

Classes are segregated by sex. At the secondary level, students are able to choose from three types of schools: general education, vocational and ___E:technical U:(https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/List_of_technical_colleges_in_Saudi_Arabia)___ , or religious.
The rate of literacy is 99% among males and 96% among females in 2020.   Youth literacy rose to approximately 99.5% for both sexes.

Higher education has expanded rapidly, with large numbers of ___E:universities and colleges being founded particularly since 2000 U:(https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/List_of_universities_and_colleges_in_Saudi_Arabia)___ .

Institutions of higher education include ___E:King Saud University U:(https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/King_Saud_University)___ at Riyadh, the ___E:Islamic University U:(https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Islamic_University_of_Madinah)___ at Medina, and the ___E:King Abdulaziz University U:(https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/King_Abdulaziz_University)___ in Jeddah. ___E:Princess Norah University U:(https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Princess_Nora_bint_Abdul_Rahman_University)___ is the largest women's university in the world. ___E:King Abdullah University of Science and Technology U:(https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/King_Abdullah_University_of_Science_and_Technology)___ , known as KAUST, is the first mixed-gender university campus in Saudi Arabia and was founded in 2009. Other colleges and universities emphasize curricula in sciences and ___E:technology U:(https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Educational_technology_in_Saudi_Arabia)___ , military studies, religion, and medicine.
Institutes devoted to Islamic studies, in particular, abound.
Women typically receive college instruction in segregated institutions.
The Academic Ranking of World Universities , known as Shanghai Ranking, ranked five Saudi institutions among its 2022 list of the 500 top universities in the world.

The ___E:QS World University Rankings U:(https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/QS_World_University_Rankings)___ lists 14 Saudi universities among the 2022 world's top universities and 23 universities among the top 100 in the ___E:Arab world U:(https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Arab_world)___ .

The 2022 list of ___E:U.S. News & World Report Best Global University Ranking U:(https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/U.S._News_%26_World_Report_Best_Global_University_Ranking)___ ranked King Abdulaziz University among the top 50 universities in the world and King Abdullah University of Science and Technology among the top 100 universities in the world.
In 2018, Saudi Arabia ranked 28th worldwide in terms of high-quality research output according to the scientific journal Nature.
Saudi Arabia spends 9% of its gross domestic product on education, compared with the global average of 5%.
Saudi Arabia was ranked 44th in the ___E:Global Innovation Index U:(https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Global_Innovation_Index)___ in 2024, up from 68th in 2019.
The Saudi education system has been accused of encouraging ___E:Islamic terrorism U:(https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Islamic_terrorism)___ , leading to reform efforts.

Following the 9/11 attacks, the government aimed to tackle the twin problems of encouraging extremism and the inadequacy of the country's university education for a modern economy, by slowly modernizing the education system through the "Tatweer" reform programme.

The Tatweer programme is reported to have a budget of approximately US$2 billion and focuses on moving teaching away from the traditional Saudi methods of memorization and rote learning towards encouraging students to analyse and problem-solve.
It also aims to create an education system which will provide a more secular and vocationally based training.

In 2021, the Washington Post reported on the measures taken by Saudi Arabia to clean textbooks from paragraphs considered ___E:antisemitic U:(https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Antisemitism)___ and ___E:sexist U:(https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Sexism)___ .

The paragraphs dealing with the punishment of ___E:homosexuality U:(https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Homosexuality)___ or same-sex relations have been deleted, as well as the expressions of admiration for the extremist martyrdom.
Antisemitic expressions and calls to fight the Jews became fewer.

David Weinberg, director of international affairs for the ___E:Anti-Defamation League U:(https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Anti-Defamation_League)___ , said that references to demonizing Jews, Christians, and Shiites have been removed from some places or have toned down. The U.S.
State Department expressed in an e-mail that it welcomed the changes.
The Saudi Ministry of Foreign Affairs supports a training programme for Saudi teachers.
Saudi Arabia has a national health care system in which the government provides free health care services through government agencies.
Saudi Arabia has been ranked among the 26 best countries in providing high quality healthcare.

The ___E:Ministry of Health U:(https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Ministry_of_Health_(Saudi_Arabia))___ is the major government agency entrusted with the provision of preventive, curative, and rehabilitative health care. The ministry's origins can be traced to 1925, when several regional health departments were established, with the first in Makkah.

The various healthcare institutions were merged to become a ministerial body in 1950.  The Health Ministry created a friendly competition between each of the districts and between different medical services and hospitals.
This idea resulted in the creation of the "Ada'a" project launched in 2016. The new system is a nationwide performance indicator, for services and hospitals.
Waiting times and other major measurements improved dramatically across the kingdom.
A new strategy has been developed by the ministry, known as Diet and Physical Activity Strategy or DPAS for short,  to address bad lifestyle choices.
The ministry advised that there should be a tax increase on unhealthy food, drink, and cigarettes.
This additional tax could be used to improve healthcare offerings.
The tax was implemented in 2017.  As part of the same strategy, calorie labels were added in 2019 to some food and drink products.

Ingredients were also listed as an aim to reduce obesity and inform citizens with health issues to manage their diet.  As part of the ongoing focus on tackling obesity, women-only gyms were allowed to open in 2017. Sports offered in each of these gyms include bodybuilding, running and swimming to maintain higher standards of health.
___E:Smoking in all age groups U:(https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Smoking_in_Saudi_Arabia)___ is widespread.
In 2009 the lowest median percentage of smokers was university students (~13.5%) while the highest was elderly people (~25%).
The study also found the median percentage of male smokers to be much higher than that of females (~26.5% for males, ~9% for females).
Before 2010, Saudi Arabia had no policies banning or restricting smoking.

The MOH has been awarded "Healthy City" certificates by the ___E:World Health Organization U:(https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/World_Health_Organization)___ (WHO) for the cities of ___E:Unayzah U:(https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Unayzah)___ and ___E:Riyadh Al Khabra U:(https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Riyadh_Al_Khabra)___ as 4th and 5th Healthy Cities in Saudi Arabia.

The WHO had earlier classified three Saudi Arabian cities, ___E:Ad Diriyah U:(https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Ad_Diriyah)___ , ___E:Jalajil U:(https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Jalajil)___ , and Al-Jamoom as "Healthy city", as part of the WHO Healthy Cities Programme.
Recently ___E:Al-Baha U:(https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Al-Baha)___ has also been classified as a healthy city to join the list of global healthy cities approved by the World Health Organization.

In May 2019, the then Saudi Minister of Health ___E:Tawfiq bin Fawzan AlRabiah U:(https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Tawfiq_bin_Fawzan_AlRabiah)___ received a global award on behalf of the Kingdom for combating smoking through social awareness, treatment, and application of regulations.

The award was presented as part of the 72nd session of the ___E:World Health Assembly U:(https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/World_Health_Assembly)___ , held in Geneva in May 2019. After becoming one of the first nations to ratify the ___E:WHO Framework Convention on Tobacco Control U:(https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/WHO_Framework_Convention_on_Tobacco_Control)___ in 2005, it plans to reduce tobacco use from 12.7% in 2017, to 5% in 2030.

Saudi Arabia has a life expectancy of 78 years (77 for males and 80 for females) according to the latest data for the year 2022 from the World Bank.  Infant mortality in 2022 was 6 per 1000 (6 for males and 5 for females).
In 2022, 71.8% of the adult population was overweight and 40.6% was obese.
The Central Department of Statistics & Information estimated the foreign population at the end of 2014 at 33% (10.1 million).
The CIA Factbook estimated that as of 2013 [update] foreign nationals living in Saudi Arabia made up about 21% of the population.

Other sources report differing estimates.  ___E:Indian U:(https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Indians_in_Saudi_Arabia)___ : 1.5 million, ___E:Pakistani U:(https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Pakistanis_in_Saudi_Arabia)___ : 1.3 million,  Egyptian: 900000 , Yemeni: 800000 , ___E:Bangladeshi U:(https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Bangladeshis_in_Saudi_Arabia)___ : 400000 , ___E:Filipino U:(https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Filipinos_in_Saudi_Arabia)___ : 500000 , Jordanian/Palestinian: 260000 , ___E:Indonesian U:(https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Indonesians_in_Saudi_Arabia)___ : 250000 , Sri Lankan: 350000 , Sudanese: 250000 , ___E:Syrian U:(https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Syrians_in_Saudi_Arabia)___ : 100000 and ___E:Turkish U:(https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Turks_in_Saudi_Arabia)___ : 80000 .
According to The Guardian , as of 2013 [update] there were more than half a million ___E:foreign-born domestic workers U:(https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Migrant_domestic_workers)___ .

Most have backgrounds in poverty and come from Africa, the Indian subcontinent and Southeast Asia.  To go to work in Saudi Arabia, they must often pay large sums to recruitment agencies in their home countries.
The agencies then handle the necessary legal paperwork.

As the Saudi population grows and oil export revenues stagnate, pressure for "Saudization" (the replacement of foreign workers with Saudis) has grown, and the Saudi government hopes to decrease the number of foreign nationals in the country.

Saudi Arabia expelled 800000 Yemenis in 1990 and 1991  and has built a ___E:Saudi–Yemen barrier U:(https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Saudi%E2%80%93Yemen_barrier)___ against an influx of illegal immigrants and against the smuggling of drugs and weapons.
In November 2013, Saudi Arabia expelled thousands of illegal Ethiopian residents from the kingdom.
Various Human Rights entities have criticized Saudi Arabia's handling of the issue.

Over 500000 ___E:undocumented migrant workers U:(https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Illegal_immigration_to_Saudi_Arabia)___ —mostly from Somalia, Ethiopia, and Yemen—have been detained and deported since 2013.  An investigation led by The Sunday Telegraph , exposed the condition of African migrants who were detained in Saudi Arabia allegedly for containing ___E:COVID-19 U:(https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Coronavirus_disease_2019)___ in the kingdom.
They were beaten, tortured, and electrocuted.
Many of the migrants died due to heatstroke or by attempting suicide, after being severely beaten and tortured.
The migrants lack proper living conditions, provision of food and water.

Foreigners cannot apply for ___E:permanent residency U:(https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Permanent_residency)___ , though a specialized ___E:Premium Residency U:(https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Premium_Residency)___ visa became available in 2019.  Only Muslims can become Saudi citizens.

Foreigners who have resided in the kingdom and hold degrees in various scientific fields may apply for Saudi citizenship,   and exception made for Palestinians who are excluded unless married to a male Saudi national, because of ___E:Arab League U:(https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Arab_League)___ instructions barring the Arab states from granting them citizenship.
Saudi Arabia is not a signatory to the ___E:1951 UN Refugee Convention U:(https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Convention_relating_to_the_Status_of_Refugees)___ .
Saudi Arabia has millennia-old attitudes and traditions, often derived from ___E:Arab civilization U:(https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/History_of_the_Arabs)___ .
Some of the major factors that influence the culture are Islamic heritage and ___E:Arab U:(https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Arab)___ traditions as well as its historical role as an ancient trade centre.
The Kingdom also has a very family-oriented culture  with an emphasis on preserving family traditions and kinship ties.

Religion is a core aspect of everyday life in Saudi Arabia; it plays a dominant role in the country's governance and legal system, and deeply influences culture and daily life, although the power of the religious establishment has been significantly eroded in the 2010s.

The ___E:Hejaz U:(https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Hejaz)___ region, where the ___E:Islamic holy cities U:(https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Holiest_sites_in_Islam)___ of Mecca and Medina are located, is the destination of the ___E:Ḥajj U:(https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Hajj)___ pilgrimage, and often deemed to be the cradle of Islam.  [i]
Islam is the state religion of Saudi Arabia.

There is no law that requires all citizens to be Muslim, but non-Muslims and many foreign and Saudi Muslims whose beliefs are deemed not to conform with the government's interpretation of Islam must practice their religion in private and are vulnerable to discrimination, harassment, detention, and, for foreigners, deportation.
Neither Saudi citizens nor guest workers have the right of ___E:freedom of religion U:(https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Freedom_of_religion)___ .
The dominant form of Islam in the kingdom—Wahhabism—arose in the central region of Najd, in the 18th century.

Proponents call the movement " ___E:Salafism U:(https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Salafism)___ ",  and believe that its teachings purify the practice of Islam of innovations or practices that deviate from the seventh-century teachings of Muhammad and ___E:his companions U:(https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Sahaba)___ .

The Saudi government has often been viewed as an active oppressor of ___E:Shia Muslims U:(https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Shia_Islam)___ because of the funding of the Wahhabi ideology which denounces the Shia faith.

Prince ___E:Bandar bin Sultan U:(https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Bandar_bin_Sultan)___ , Saudi ambassador to the United States, stated: "The time is not far off in the Middle East when it will be literally 'God help the Shia'.
More than a billion Sunnis have simply had enough of them."

Saudi Arabia is one of the few countries that have " ___E:religious police U:(https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Committee_for_the_Promotion_of_Virtue_and_the_Prevention_of_Vice_(Saudi_Arabia))___ " (known as Haia or Mutaween ), who patrol the streets " ___E:enjoining good and forbidding wrong U:(https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Enjoining_good_and_forbidding_wrong)___ " by enforcing ___E:dress codes U:(https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Clothing_laws_by_country)___ , strict ___E:separation of men and women U:(https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Sex_segregation)___ , attendance at prayer ( salat ) five times each day, the ban on alcohol, and other aspects of Sharia.
However, since 2016 the power of religious police was curbed, which barred them from pursuing, questioning, requesting identification or arresting suspects.

In the privacy of homes, behaviour can be far looser, and reports from ___E:WikiLeaks U:(https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/WikiLeaks)___ indicate that low ranked members of the ruling Saudi Royal family indulge in parties with alcohol, drugs, and prostitutes.

Throughout history, women did not have equal rights to men in the kingdom; the ___E:U.S. State Department U:(https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/U.S._State_Department)___ considers the Saudi Arabian government's discrimination against women a "significant problem" and notes that women have few political rights because of the government's discriminatory policies.
However, since Mohammed bin Salman was appointed Crown Prince in 2017, a series of social reforms have been witnessed regarding women's rights.
Under previous Saudi law, all females were required to have a male guardian ( wali ), typically a father, brother, husband, or uncle ( mahram ).
In 2019, this law was partially amended to exclude women over 21 years old from the requirement of a male guardian.
The amendment also granted women rights in relation to the guardianship of minor children.
Previously, girls and women were forbidden from travelling, conducting official business, or undergoing certain medical procedures without permission from their male guardians.
In 2019, Saudi Arabia allowed women to travel abroad, register for divorce or marriage, and apply for official documents without the permission of a male guardian.

In 2006, ___E:Wajeha al-Huwaider U:(https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Wajeha_al-Huwaider)___ , a leading Saudi feminist and journalist said "Saudi women are weak, no matter how high their status, even the 'pampered' ones among them, because they have no law to protect them from attack by anyone."  Following this, Saudi Arabia implemented the anti- ___E:domestic violence U:(https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Domestic_violence_in_Saudi_Arabia)___ law in 2014.  Furthermore, between 2017 and 2020, the country addressed issues of mobility, sexual harassment, pensions, and employment-discrimination protections.    al-Huwaider and other female activists have applauded the general direction in which the country was headed.

Women face discrimination in the courts, where the testimony of one man equals that of two women ___E:in family and inheritance law U:(https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Legal_system_of_Saudi_Arabia#Family_law)___ .
Polygamy is permitted for men,  and men have a unilateral right to divorce their wives ( ___E:talaq U:(https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Divorce_(Islamic))___ ) without needing any legal justification.

Historically, a woman could only obtain a divorce with the consent of her husband or judicially if her husband has harmed her;  however, in 2022, women were granted the right to initiate divorce without the approval of a legal guardian under the new Personal Status Law.  With regard to inheritance law, the Quran specifies that fixed portions of the deceased's estate must be left to the Qur'anic heirs  and generally, female heirs receive half the portion of male heirs.

Saudi Wahhabism is hostile to any reverence given to historical or religious places of significance for fear that it may give rise to ___E:'shirk' U:(https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Shirk_(Islam))___ (idolatry), and the most significant historic Muslim sites (in Mecca and Medina) are located in the western Saudi region of the Hejaz.

As a consequence, under Saudi rule an estimated 95% of Mecca's historic buildings, most over a thousand years old, ___E:have been demolished U:(https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Destruction_of_early_Islamic_heritage_sites_in_Saudi_Arabia)___ for religious reasons.

Critics claim that over the last 50 years, 300 historic sites linked to Muhammad, his family or companions have been lost,  leaving fewer than 20 structures remaining in Mecca that date back to the time of Muhammad.

Demolished structures include the mosque originally built by Muhammad's daughter ___E:Fatima U:(https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Fatima_bint_Muhammad)___ , and other mosques founded by ___E:Abu Bakr U:(https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Abu_Bakr)___ (Muhammad's father-in-law and the first ___E:caliph U:(https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Caliph)___ ), ___E:Umar U:(https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Umar_ibn_al-Khattab)___ (the second caliph), ___E:Ali U:(https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Ali_ibn_Abi_Talib)___ (Muhammad's son-in-law and the fourth caliph), and ___E:Salman al-Farsi U:(https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Salman_al-Farsi)___ (another of Muhammad's companions).

Eight cultural sites in Saudi Arabia are designated as ___E:UNESCO World Heritage Sites U:(https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/UNESCO_World_Heritage_Sites)___ : Al-Hijr Archaeological Site ( ___E:Madâin Sâlih U:(https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Mada%27in_Saleh)___ );  the ___E:Turaif district U:(https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Turaif_district)___ in Diriyah;  Historic Jeddah, the Gate to Mecca;  ___E:Al-Ahsa Oasis U:(https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Al-Ahsa_Oasis)___ ;  ___E:Rock Art in the Hail Region U:(https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Rock_Art_in_the_Ha%27il_Region)___ ;  ___E:Ḥimā Cultural Area U:(https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Bir_Hima_Rock_Petroglyphs_and_Inscriptions)___ ;  ___E:'Uruq Bani Ma'arid U:(https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/%27Uruq_Bani_Ma%27arid)___ ;  and ___E:Qaryat al-Faw U:(https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Qaryat_al-Faw)___ .

Ten other sites submitted requests for recognition to UNESCO in 2015.  There are six elements inscribed on ___E:UNESCO's Intangible Cultural Heritage of Humanity list U:(https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/UNESCO_Intangible_Cultural_Heritage_Lists)___ :  ___E:Al-Qatt Al-Asiri U:(https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Al-Qatt_Al-Asiri)___ , female traditional interior wall decoration in Asir; ___E:Almezmar U:(https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Almezmar_in_Saudi_Arabia)___ , drumming and dancing with sticks; ___E:Falconry U:(https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Falconry)___ , a living human heritage; ___E:Arabic coffee U:(https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Arabic_coffee)___ , a symbol of generosity; ___E:Majlis U:(https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Majlis)___ , a cultural and social space; Alardah Alnajdiyah, dance, drumming and poetry in Saudi Arabia.

In June 2014, the Council of Ministers approved a law that gives the ___E:Saudi Commission for Tourism and National Heritage U:(https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Saudi_Commission_for_Tourism_and_National_Heritage)___ the means to protect Saudi Arabia's ancient relics and historic sites.

Within the framework of the 2016 National Transformation Programme, also known as ___E:Saudi Vision 2030 U:(https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Saudi_Vision_2030)___ , the kingdom allocated 900 million euros to preserve its historical and cultural heritage.
Saudi Arabia also participates in the International Alliance for the Protection of Heritage in Conflict Areas, created in March 2017, with a contribution of 18.5 million euros.
In 2017, Crown Prince Mohammad bin Salman promised to return Saudi Arabia to the "moderate Islam" of the era before the 1979 Iranian revolution.

A new centre, the King Salman Complex for the Prophet's Hadith, was established that year to monitor interpretations of the Prophet Mohammed's hadiths to prevent them being used to justifying terrorism.
In March 2018, the Crown Prince met the Archbishop of Canterbury during a visit to the UK, pledging to promote interfaith dialogue.
In Riyadh the following month King Salman met the head of the Vatican's Pontifical Council for Interreligious Dialogue.
In July 2019, UNESCO signed a letter with the Saudi Minister of Culture in which Saudi Arabia contributed US$25 million to UNESCO for the preservation of heritage.
On November 5, 2024, archeologists published the news of an ancient city discovered in the Saudi oasis of ___E:Khaybar U:(https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Khaybar)___ .
The city named al-Natah, that dates back some 4,000 years, was inhabited during the Bronze Age around 2,400 BC, and had about 500 houses.
Not far, a cluster of graves was found, within them metal weapons.
Saudi Arabian dress strictly follows the principles of ___E:hijab U:(https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Hijab)___ (the Islamic principle of modesty, especially in dress).
The predominantly loose and flowing, but covering, garments are suited to Saudi Arabia's desert climate.

Traditionally, men usually wear a white ankle-length garment woven from wool or cotton (known as a ___E:thawb U:(https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Thawb)___ ), with a ___E:keffiyeh U:(https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Keffiyeh)___ (a large checkered square of cotton held in place by an ___E:agal U:(https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Agal_(accessory))___ ) or a ghutra (a plain white square made of a finer cotton, also held in place by an ___E:agal U:(https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Agal_(accessory))___ ) worn on the head. For rare chilly days, Saudi men wear a camel-hair cloak ( ___E:bisht U:(https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Bisht_(clothing))___ ) over the top. In public, women are required to wear a black ___E:abaya U:(https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Abaya)___ or other black clothing that covers everything under the neck with the exception of their hands and feet, although most women cover their head in respect of their religion.
This requirement applies to non-Muslim women too and failure to abide can result in police action, particularly in more conservative areas of the country.
Women's clothes are often decorated with tribal motifs, coins, sequins, metallic thread, and appliques.
During the 1970s, cinemas were numerous in the kingdom although they were seen as contrary to Wahhabi norms.

During the ___E:Islamic revival U:(https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Islamic_revival)___ movement in the 1980s, and as a political response to an increase in Islamist activism including the 1979 seizure of the Grand Mosque in Mecca, the government closed all cinemas and theatres.
However, with King Abdullah and King Salman's reforms, cinemas re-opened,  including one in ___E:KAUST U:(https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/King_Abdullah_University_of_Science_and_Technology)___ .
From the 18th century onward, Wahhabi fundamentalism discouraged artistic development inconsistent with its teaching.

In addition, Sunni Islamic prohibition of creating representations of people have limited the visual arts, which tend to be dominated by ___E:geometric U:(https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Islamic_geometric_patterns)___ , ___E:floral U:(https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Arabesque)___ , and abstract designs and by ___E:calligraphy U:(https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Islamic_calligraphy)___ .
With the advent of the oil-wealth in the 20th century came exposure to outside influences, such as Western housing styles, furnishings, and clothes.
Music and dance have always been part of Saudi life. Traditional music is generally associated with poetry and is sung collectively.

Instruments include the ___E:rabābah U:(https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Rebab)___ , an instrument not unlike a three-string fiddle, and various types of percussion instruments, such as the ṭabl (drum) and the ṭār (tambourine).
The national dance is a native sword dance known as ___E:ardah U:(https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Ardah)___ .
Originating from Najd, it involves lines or circles of men and singing poetry.
Bedouin poetry, known as nabaṭī, is popular.

Censorship has limited the development of Saudi literature, although several ___E:Saudi novelists and poets U:(https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/List_of_Saudi_Arabian_writers)___ have achieved critical and popular acclaim in the Arab world—albeit generating official hostility in their home country.

These include ___E:Ghazi Algosaibi U:(https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Ghazi_Algosaibi)___ , ___E:Mansour al-Nogaidan U:(https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Mansour_al-Nogaidan)___ , ___E:Abdelrahman Munif U:(https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Abdelrahman_Munif)___ , ___E:Turki al-Hamad U:(https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Turki_al-Hamad)___ , and ___E:Rajaa al-Sanea U:(https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Rajaa_al-Sanea)___ .
In 2016, the General Entertainment Authority (GEA) was formed to oversee the expansion of the Saudi entertainment sector.
The first concerts in Riyadh for 25 years took place the following year.  Other events since the GEA's creation have included comedy shows, professional wrestling events, and monster truck rallies.
In 2018 the first public cinema opened after a ban of 35 years, with plans to have more than 2000 screens running by 2030.

Developments in the arts in 2018 included Saudi Arabia's debut appearances at the ___E:Cannes Film Festival U:(https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Cannes_Film_Festival)___ and the ___E:Venice Biennale U:(https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Venice_Biennale)___ .

Television was introduced in Saudi Arabia in 1954. Saudi Arabia is a major market for ___E:pan-Arab U:(https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Pan-Arab_States)___ satellite and ___E:pay-TV U:(https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Pay_television)___ .

It controls the largest share of the pan-Arab broadcasting market; among the major Saudi-owned broadcasting companies are the ___E:Middle East Broadcasting Centre U:(https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/MBC_Group)___ , ___E:Rotana U:(https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Rotana_Group)___ , and the ___E:Saudi Broadcasting Authority U:(https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Saudi_Broadcasting_Authority)___ .

The Saudi government ___E:closely monitors media and restricts it U:(https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Censorship_in_Saudi_Arabia)___ under official state law. Changes have been made to lessen these restrictions; however, some government-led efforts to control information have also drawn international attention.
As of 2022, ___E:Reporters Without Borders U:(https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Reporters_Without_Borders)___ rates the kingdom's press a "very serious" situation.
Most of the early newspapers in the Persian Gulf region were established in Saudi Arabia.

The first newspaper founded in the country and in the Persian Gulf area is Al Fallah , which was launched in 1920,  and the first English-language newspaper is Arab News , which was launched in 1975.  All of the ___E:newspapers published in Saudi Arabia U:(https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/List_of_newspapers_in_Saudi_Arabia)___ are privately owned.

According to ___E:World Bank U:(https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/World_Bank)___ , as of 2020, 98% of the population of Saudi Arabia are internet users which puts it in the 8th rank among countries with the highest percentage of internet users.
Saudi Arabia has one of the fastest ___E:5G U:(https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/5G)___ internet speeds in the world.
The kingdom is the 27th largest market for ___E:e-commerce U:(https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/E-commerce)___ with a revenue of US$8 billion in 2021.

___E:Saudi Arabian cuisine U:(https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Saudi_Arabian_cuisine)___ is similar to that of the surrounding countries in the Arabian Peninsula and the wider Arab world, and has influenced and been influenced by Turkish, Indian, Persian, and African food. ___E:Islamic dietary laws U:(https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Islamic_dietary_laws)___ are enforced: pork is not allowed, and other animals are slaughtered in accordance with ___E:halal U:(https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Halal)___ . ___E:Kebabs U:(https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Kebab)___ and ___E:falafel U:(https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Falafel)___ are popular, as is ___E:shawarma U:(https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Shawarma)___ , a marinated grilled meat dish of lamb, mutton, or chicken. ___E:Kabsa U:(https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Kabsa)___ , a rice dish with lamb, chicken, fish, or shrimp, is among the national dishes as is ___E:mandi U:(https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Mandi_(food))___ .
Flat, unleavened ___E:taboon bread U:(https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Taboon_bread)___ is a staple of virtually every meal, as are dates, fresh fruit, yoghurt, and hummus.

Coffee, served in the ___E:Arabic style U:(https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Arabic_coffee)___ , is the traditional beverage, but tea and various fruit juices are popular as well.  The earliest substantiated evidence of either ___E:coffee drinking U:(https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/History_of_coffee)___ or knowledge of the coffee tree is from the 15th century, in the ___E:Sufi U:(https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Sufi)___ monasteries of Arabia.
___E:Football U:(https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Football_in_Saudi_Arabia)___ is the national sport in Saudi Arabia.

The ___E:Saudi Arabia national football team U:(https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Saudi_Arabia_national_football_team)___ is considered one of Asia's most successful national teams, having reached a joint record six ___E:AFC Asian Cup U:(https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/AFC_Asian_Cup)___ finals, winning three of those finals ( ___E:1984 U:(https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/1984_AFC_Asian_Cup_final)___ , ___E:1988 U:(https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/1988_AFC_Asian_Cup_final)___ , and ___E:1996 U:(https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/1996_AFC_Asian_Cup_final)___ ) and ___E:having qualified for the World Cup U:(https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Saudi_Arabia_at_the_FIFA_World_Cup)___ four consecutive times ever since debuting at the 1994 tournament.

In the ___E:1994 FIFA World Cup U:(https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/1994_FIFA_World_Cup)___ under the leadership of ___E:Jorge Solari U:(https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Jorge_Solari)___ , Saudi Arabia beat both Belgium and Morocco in the group stage before failing to defeat Sweden in the round of 16. During the ___E:1992 FIFA Confederations Cup U:(https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/1992_King_Fahd_Cup)___ , which was played in Saudi Arabia, the country reached the ___E:final U:(https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/1992_King_Fahd_Cup_Final)___ , losing 1–3 to Argentina.

Scuba diving, windsurfing, sailing, and basketball (which is played by both men and women) are also popular with the ___E:Saudi Arabian national basketball team U:(https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Saudi_Arabia_national_basketball_team)___ winning bronze at the ___E:1999 Asian Championship U:(https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/1999_ABC_Championship)___ .
More traditional sports such as ___E:horse racing U:(https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Horse_racing)___ and ___E:camel racing U:(https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Camel_racing)___ are also popular.

The annual King's Camel Race, begun in 1974, is one of the sport's most important contests and attracts animals and riders from throughout the region. ___E:Falconry U:(https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Falconry)___ is another traditional pursuit.

___E:Women's sport U:(https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Women%27s_sport_in_Saudi_Arabia)___ is controversial because of the suppression of female participation in sport by conservative Islamic religious authorities,  however the restrictions have eased.
Until 2018 women were not permitted in sport stadiums.
Segregated seating, allowing women to enter, has been developed in three stadiums across major cities.

Since 2020, the progress of women's integration into the Saudi sport scene began to develop rapidly.   25 Saudi sport federations established a national women's team,  including a national ___E:football U:(https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Saudi_Arabia_women%27s_national_football_team)___ and ___E:basketball team U:(https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Saudi_Arabia_women%27s_national_basketball_team)___ .

In November 2020, the ___E:Saudi Arabian Football Federation U:(https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Saudi_Arabian_Football_Federation)___ announced the launch of the first nationwide ___E:Saudi women's premier league U:(https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Saudi_Women%27s_Premier_League)___ .
In its vision for modernization, the nation has introduced many international sporting events, bringing sports stars to the kingdom.

However, in August 2019, the kingdom's strategy received criticism for appearing as a method of ___E:sportswashing U:(https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Sportswashing_in_Saudi_Arabia)___ soon after Saudi's US-based 2018 lobbying campaign foreign registration documentations got published online.

The documents showed Saudi Arabia as allegedly implementing a sportswashing strategy, including meetings and official calls with authorities of associations like ___E:Major League Soccer U:(https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Major_League_Soccer)___ , ___E:World Wrestling Entertainment U:(https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/WWE_in_Saudi_Arabia)___ , and the ___E:National Basketball Association U:(https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/National_Basketball_Association)___ .
In December 2024, Saudi Arabia was confirmed as host of the ___E:2034 FIFA World Cup U:(https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/2034_FIFA_World_Cup)___ .
Developments of stadiums to be used for the event are ongoing.
There are reportedly 11 new stadiums being built and airports are scheduled to be expanded to accommodate the expected influx of passengers.
